correctness.rationale: The exact monomial moments are obtained from normalized planar area. A uniform phase-independent difference bound between beta and gamma integrals gives the reciprocal-moment estimate. Its error sums to an inverse-scale contribution, and a uniformly dominated Riemann-sum argument establishes locally uniform complex boundary scaling. Gamma nonvanishing exactly preserves the period group. The diagonal cluster interval follows from a second gamma multiplier, and Laplace-transform uniqueness plus periodic averaging proves projective injectivity. Constant weights recover the classical Bergman kernel. Numerical beta-moment and quadrature checks passed; they are supplementary, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The one-sided doubling class naturally permits strong radial oscillation, so boundary tangent uniqueness is a motivated structural property not settled by sharp norm bounds. The theorem gives a complete constant-versus-nonconstant classification for every positive continuous periodic profile, constructs the entire circle of positive-definite tangent kernels, proves that scalar normalization does not remove the phenomenon, and identifies a nondegenerate diagonal cluster interval. This is a substantive boundary-universality obstruction, not an isolated arbitrary computation.
